title: Additive restriction of conductor tensor sections
statement: Let $Y$ be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme] whose underlying space is the union of finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$, each given its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $Z\subset Y$ be the reduced closed subscheme supported on $Z_2\cup\cdots\cup Z_r$, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $\mathcal I_1$ be the image of $\mathcal I|_{Z_1}$ in $\mathcal O_{Z_1}$. For any invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and any $m\ge0$, restriction is an isomorphism $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal I\mathcal M^{\otimes m})\cong\Gamma(Z_1,\mathcal I_1(\mathcal M|_{Z_1})^{\otimes m})$. More precisely the additive restriction map between the tensor products of the ideal modules and the invertible tensor powers is bijective, and commutes with the two inclusions into the ambient tensor powers. No claim about extensions as ambient sections or their nonvanishing loci is included.

source.place: Varieties Remark 09NW and Lemma 09NX, displayed conductor equality

proof.text: Compare tensorPullback with the source-library pullback using uniqueness of left adjoints. Use the already proved nonempty_pullback_tensorPow_iso (the induction of the tensor pullback comparison) and the explicitly constructed tensorPowCongr to obtain e. Transport the proved IsInvertible.pullback instance through the left-adjoint comparison to obtain invertibility of tensorPullback M.

Apply conductorIdealZeroIntersection with this e and evaluate the resulting morphism ρ on the top open. Its section map is bijective. Tensoring the ideal inclusion with the invertible tensor power is monic; imageMonoIsoSource and evaluation give an additive isomorphism p from the original ideal tensor sections to image sections.

Apply ideal_tensor_image_comparison to obtain the additive isomorphism q from the component image sections to the extended ideal tensor sections. Set r=q composed with ρ(top) composed with p. Bijectivity follows by composition. Evaluate the commutative square for ρ, use imageMonoIsoSource_inv_ι, cancel e.hom against e.inv, then apply the unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app equation. These equalities prove precisely compatibility with the canonical adjunction unit.

lean.statement: theorem conductor_sections_restriction {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced Y] {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (C : ι → Scheme.{u}) (i : ∀ b : ι, C b ⟶ Y) [∀ b : ι, IsReduced (C b)] [∀ b : ι, IsClosedImmersion (i b)] (hcomponents : ∀ b : ι, Set.range (i b) ∈ irreducibleComponents Y) (hdistinct : Function.Injective fun b : ι => Set.range (i b)) (hcover : (⋃ b : ι, Set.range (i b)) = Set.univ) (a : ι) {Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced Z] (j : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hZ : Set.range j = ⋃ b : ι, ⋃ (_ : b ≠ a), Set.range (i b)) (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] (m : ℕ) : let N := M.tensorPow m let N₁ := (tensorPullback (i a)).obj N let adj₁ := Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (i a)) let res₁ : Γ(N, ⊤) → Γ(N₁, ⊤) := fun t ↦ (adj₁.unit.app N).val.app (op ⊤) t let I := j.ker let I₁ := I.comap (i a) let μ : I.toModules ⊗ N ⟶ N := I.toModulesι ▷ N ≫ (λ_ N).hom let μ₁ : I₁.toModules ⊗ N₁ ⟶ N₁ := I₁.toModulesι ▷ N₁ ≫ (λ_ N₁).hom ∃ r : Γ(I.toModules ⊗ N, ⊤) →+ Γ(I₁.toModules ⊗ N₁, ⊤), Function.Bijective r ∧ ∀ s, μ₁.app ⊤ (r s) = res₁ (μ.app ⊤ s)
